title: I’m a maths teacher and chess coach. I built 6 apps in 2 weeks with AI — 3 are now on Google Play
author: TallMiddle7540
selftext:
I'm a maths teacher and Chinese chess coach, and I've spent the last two weeks building six apps with AI. Three are now live on Google Play under my little studio, ElephantLogix.



The three live ones are Arrow Dungeon (an arrow puzzle game), Liangshan Banqi (Chinese dark chess), and Pi-Rex (maths practice with a dinosaur buddy). The other three aren't live yet.



The AI work goes beyond coding. I've been using Claude and Codex for development, AI tools for artwork and audio, and AI assistance to build the website. I still choose the ideas and rules, test the builds, and decide what needs fixing. Calling it “AI did everything” would leave out a lot of that work.



One part I'm particularly interested in is bringing my teaching background into the games. With Banqi, the rules and explanations need to be right. With Pi-Rex, a maths question needs more than a nice-looking screen: the answer and explanation have to make sense to a learner. Those are things I need to check myself, however convincing the generated result looks.



I'm also learning that getting a game running and getting it ready for players are different jobs. Store submissions, testing, artwork cleanup and setting up a website all sit around the actual game. And now that three are published, I have a new question: will people enjoy them enough to come back?



I'm documenting this as an ongoing experiment, including what works and what doesn't. Publishing three games is a milestone; it isn't proof of a successful business yet.



For context and screenshots, my site is [https://elephantlogix.com](https://elephantlogix.com) — I'm the developer, so this is my own work.



For others building with AI: what has taken you the most effort after the first playable version? And would a breakdown of the coding workflow, art/audio tools, or Google Play publishing process be most useful?

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: 6 apps in 2 weeks isn’t the flex you think it is

comments.author: crackedpotstudio
comments.body: The art of coding with AI is to iterate as much as possible and design an awesome and good working product. Mindlessly cranking out as much as possible only creates a bunch of slop nobody is going to use snd you only please the anti AI crowd.
